key_insight: Elevated freestream turbulence improves mean airfoil performance but masks bistable post-stall switching between two partially separated flow states.
engineering_relevance: Post-stall load assessment should account for state switching and occupancy rather than relying only on mean lift and standard deviation.
method: Measured time-resolved surface pressures on a thick, cambered FFA-W3-301 airfoil at Reynolds numbers of 125,000–275,000.
Compared clean inflow with three passive turbulence grids to separate turbulence-intensity and integral-length-scale effects.
Used conditional pressure averages and proper orthogonal decomposition to identify separation-front states.
evidence_signal: At the highest tested Reynolds number, switching persisted across up to 9° of angle of attack, with nearly turbulence-independent lift levels but different state occupancies.
watch_item: Results concern one airfoil section over a limited Reynolds-number range; transfer to full-scale, three-dimensional wings requires validation.
paper_title: Bistability in the stalling behavior of thick, cambered airfoils under elevated freestream turbulence
